notes: Use Uber/Ola (air-conditioned) or black-and-yellow taxis (metered). Suburban trains are packed; the first carriage is for women. Metro Line 3 has linked Colaba, Bandra and the airport since 2025. Allow 45 to 90 minutes to the airport in traffic.
JUNE TO SEPTEMBER MONSOON: hours of downpour daily, flooding, and the Elephanta ferry is sometimes cancelled. Bring an umbrella and sandals. The city is green and cool (28°C), and hotels are cheap.
The e-Visa (30 days) is applied for online. Carry cash in INR (with 500 notes in small change); UPI is limited for foreigners, and cards are accepted at larger places.
Street food: vada pav 20 to 30 INR, pav bhaji 100 INR, bhel puri 60 INR. Irani cafe breakfast 300 INR; restaurants 600 to 1,000 INR. Stick to bottled water and be careful with ice and raw salad.
Elephanta is closed on Mondays and Britannia on Sundays. Visit Haji Ali at low tide. Museums open at 10:15.
Visit Dharavi only with a responsible company (Reality Tours). A Bollywood studio tour (Film City) costs 2,000+ INR.

stops.name: Gateway of India
stops.tips: A 1924 basalt triumphal arch opposite the Taj Mahal Palace hotel. Come in the morning for pigeons and boats.

stops.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya
stops.tips: The former Prince of Wales Museum: an Indo-Saracenic dome, miniature paintings and an audio guide.

stops.name: Kala Ghoda Art District
stops.tips: Galleries, the free Jehangir Art Gallery and Rhythm House. The festival is held in February.

stops.name: Leopold Cafe
stops.tips: A Parsi cafe dating from 1871 (of Shantaram fame). Order a beer and chicken tikka; the bullet marks are still on the walls.

stops.name: Colaba Causeway
stops.tips: A street market for bargaining, cheap clothes and souvenirs.

backups.name: Bademiya Colaba
backups.tips: A late-night kebab stand behind the Taj: seekh kebab and roti.

backups.name: Afghan Church Colaba
backups.tips: An 1858 church, quieter than Kala Ghoda.

stops.name: Elephanta Caves
stops.tips: In monsoon the ferry is sometimes cancelled (rough seas June to August). If the weather allows, take the first boat at 09:00 and bring a raincoat.

stops.name: Gateway of India Ferry Pier
stops.tips: For the return trip. Elephanta has only snacks.

stops.name: Britannia & Co Ballard Estate
stops.tips: A Parsi cafe from 1923. Try the berry pulao. Closed on Sundays and shuts at 16:00.

stops.name: Marine Drive
stops.tips: The "Queen's Necklace", a 3.6 km seafront. Walk from Nariman Point to Chowpatty at sunset as the street lamps come on.

stops.name: Girgaon Chowpatty Beach
stops.tips: Bhel puri and pav bhaji stalls line the beach. Swimming is not allowed.

backups.name: Kanheri Caves Sanjay Gandhi
backups.tips: If the ferry is cancelled: 109 Buddhist caves in the national park, near Borivali.

backups.name: Cafe Mondegar Colaba
backups.tips: A cafe with Mario Miranda murals. Beer and sandwiches.

stops.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
stops.tips: A UNESCO-listed Victorian Gothic station handling 3 million passengers a day. See it from outside and in the main hall.

stops.name: Dhobi Ghat Mahalaxmi
stops.tips: The world's largest open-air laundry. View it from the bridge; a tour costs 200 INR.

stops.name: Haji Ali Dargah
stops.tips: A tomb in the sea dating from 1431. The causeway is walkable at low tide. Expect loudspeaker chanting; cover your head.

stops.name: Haji Ali Juice Centre
stops.tips: The legendary juice stall across the way. Try the sitaphal (custard apple) cream.

stops.name: Mani Bhavan Gandhi Museum
stops.tips: Gandhi's Mumbai home from 1917 to 1934, in Gamdevi. Free entry.

backups.name: Mahalaxmi Temple
backups.tips: A seaside temple, a substitute for Haji Ali at high tide.

stops.name: Dharavi Slum Tour Reality Tours
stops.tips: Asia's largest slum, with recycling, leather and pottery workshops. A responsible tour: no photos, and 80% of proceeds go to the community.

stops.name: Mahim Dargah
stops.tips: A 15th-century shrine next to Dharavi.

stops.name: Sarvi Byculla
stops.tips: Seekh kebab and khichda since the 1920s, in Byculla.

stops.name: Banganga Tank
stops.tips: A sacred tank on Malabar Hill dating from 1127, a village-like corner of Mumbai.

stops.name: Hanging Gardens Malabar Hill
stops.tips: Topiary shrubs and views of Marine Drive. The shoe-shaped house is in Kamala Nehru Park.

backups.name: Bhau Daji Lad Museum Byculla
backups.tips: The city's oldest museum in Byculla, a substitute for Banganga.

backups.name: Swati Snacks Tardeo
backups.tips: A Gujarati street-food restaurant: panki and dahi puri.

stops.name: Mount Mary Basilica
stops.tips: A basilica on Bandra hill. The Bandra Fair takes place in September.

stops.name: Bandstand Promenade
stops.tips: A seafront walk past Shah Rukh Khan's Mannat, with views of the Sea Link from Bandra Fort.

stops.name: Candies Bandra
stops.tips: A garden cafe serving Parsi and Goan dishes, a city favourite.

stops.name: Linking Road & Hill Road
stops.tips: A street market for cheap shoes and clothes.

stops.name: Carter Road Sunset
stops.tips: A rocky seafront promenade with Bandra's young crowd and cafes.

backups.name: Elco Bandra
backups.tips: A Hill Road institution for pani puri and chaat.

backups.name: Pali Village Cafe
backups.tips: An ivy-covered cafe on Pali Hill, best in the evening.

stops.name: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
stops.tips: Monsoon greenery and waterfalls. The paths are muddy, so wear proper shoes.

stops.name: Kanheri Caves
stops.tips: 109 Buddhist caves dating from the 1st century BC to the 10th century. The park bus takes 20 minutes.

stops.name: Global Vipassana Pagoda
stops.tips: The world's largest stone dome, in Gorai. Take the ferry (from Borivali West); meditation is offered.

stops.name: Juhu Beach
stops.tips: The Bollywood beach: pav bhaji and gola stalls, and sunset. Swimming is not allowed.

stops.name: Prithvi Cafe Juhu
stops.tips: A theatre cafe with Irish coffee and keema pav. Come on a play night.

backups.name: Anand Stall Juhu
backups.tips: Street-side vada pav and dosa opposite Mithibai College.

backups.name: ISKCON Juhu
backups.tips: A Hare Krishna temple, a nearby substitute for the pagoda.

days.theme: Fort morning and a gentle farewell

stops.name: Asiatic Society Library Town Hall
stops.tips: An 1830 neoclassical building on Horniman Circle. Its steps are a Bollywood set.

stops.name: Horniman Circle Gardens
stops.tips: A garden and St Thomas Cathedral (1718).

stops.name: Kyani & Co Marine Lines
stops.tips: A 1904 Irani cafe. Order bun maska and chai, or keema, for a farewell.

stops.name: Ashok Vada Pav Dadar
stops.tips: The city's most famous vada pav (potato fritter in a bun), by Kirti College.

stops.name: Mumbai Airport Metro/Taxi
stops.tips: Uber or Ola takes 45 to 90 minutes in traffic. Farewell.

backups.name: Yazdani Bakery Fort
backups.tips: An Irani bakery from 1953: brun maska.

backups.name: Flora Fountain
backups.tips: The fountain on Fort's square, a substitute for the gardens.
